cuts.raw_narration: Gon, a boy in a green outfit with spiky black hair, charges through a blinding white flash and lands a punch on Gerreta, who ends up face-down on the forest path. Hisoka, the pale clown-like man with pink hair, stands calmly on the trail holding out the badge he'd taken, and coolly tells the beaten opponent he'll let him live for now — he can have it back only when he can punch him in the face like Gon just did. Until then, Hisoka will hold onto it for him.

Amori, the brother in the blue shirt and green-and-white cap, swaggers up to Gon in the mossy forest and tells him to just hand the badge over so he won't get hurt. Gon quietly calls him an idiot. In a blur of motion he slams a fist into Amori's gut — Amori doubles over, eyes bulging, and drops flat onto the tree roots, motionless. The other two brothers, one in a yellow striped shirt and one in an orange beanie and red turtleneck, freeze in shock, sweating and gaping down at their unconscious sibling as Gon stands calmly over him.

As the two remaining Amori brothers snarl about their unbeatable formation, Killua — the pale boy with spiky silver hair — appears silently behind the one in the orange beanie and slides his long, claw-sharp fingernails up against the man's throat. Smiling playfully, Killua leans in close and whispers that his fingers cut better than any knife. The terrified brother trembles and sweats as Killua calmly reads off his badge number, then flicks it away into the trees.

Deeper in the cave, chopped-up pieces of a green snake lie in pools of red blood on the sandy floor. Kurapika stares in horror at Gon, who has collapsed unconscious, his body covered in dozens of dark snake bites. Leorio, kneeling in the lantern light with his round glasses and white shirt, grimly identifies them as viper bites and, sweating hard, pulls out a small knife and bandages to stop the bleeding.

A voice from deeper in the cave warns them they aren't getting out so easily. Bourbon, the snake charmer, sits cross-legged in the shadows beside a small lantern, a black snake with a piercing yellow eye coiled up next to his face. He explains that a mass of vipers will swarm anyone who tries to leave, that the bites paralyze and then kill, and that this is his trap. Leorio desperately offers him every badge they have if he'll just let them out. Bourbon slowly tells them not to bother — Ponzu is already dead — and the shot lingers on his cold, wide-eyed stare and the coiled snake, closing on a chilling cliffhanger.
